This page gives the statistical map shared by the Bayesian linear regression
(BLR) models in `sblr`. It separates the regression model and prior family from
the data representation used to evaluate the likelihood. Detailed
summary-statistic, overlap, operator, annotation-prior, and multi-trait state
derivations live on their dedicated methods pages.

## Single-trait regression

For a centered phenotype \(y\in\mathbb R^N\), genotype matrix
\(X\in\mathbb R^{N\times M}\), marker effects \(b\in\mathbb R^M\), and residual
vector \(e\), the single-trait model is

$$
y=Xb+e,
\qquad
e\sim N(0,v_eI_N).
$$

Here \(v_e\) is the residual variance. The fitted genetic values are \(Xb\),
and their variance is denoted \(v_g\). A global active-marker effect-variance
scale is denoted \(v_b\).

### BayesC

BayesC uses a point mass at zero and one non-null normal distribution:

$$
d_j\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\pi_j),
$$

$$
b_j=0\quad(d_j=0),
\qquad
b_j\mid d_j=1\sim N(0,v_bq_j).
$$

In the ordinary model, \(\pi_j=\pi\) and \(q_j=1\). Annotation-informed prior
architectures may change marker inclusion probabilities or relative non-null
effect variance without changing the Gaussian regression likelihood.

### BayesR

BayesR replaces the single non-null distribution with a finite mixture. Use
the theoretical indexing convention

$$
\gamma_0=0,
\qquad
\gamma_k>0,\quad k=1,\ldots,K.
$$

Then

$$
c_j\sim\operatorname{Categorical}(P_{j0},\ldots,P_{jK}),
$$

$$
b_j=0\quad(c_j=0),
\qquad
b_j\mid c_j=k>0\sim N(0,\gamma_kq_jv_b).
$$

The \(\gamma_k\) ladder contains known relative component multipliers, \(q_j\)
is a marker-specific relative variance multiplier, and \(v_b\) carries the
global active-effect variance scale. In current R inputs, the first element of
`mixture_var` is the null multiplier; its one-based R position represents the
theoretical component \(k=0\).

BayesRC/SBayesRC retains the BayesR effect mixture and makes marker component
probabilities annotation dependent. Log-variance models retain global
probability architecture and learn \(q_j\) from annotations. See
[Annotation-Informed Priors](annotation_priors.qmd).

## Multi-trait regression

For \(T\) traits, collect phenotypes, marker effects, and observation-level
residuals in matrices:

$$
Y=XB+E_Y,
$$

where \(Y\in\mathbb R^{N\times T}\), \(B\in\mathbb R^{M\times T}\), and
\(E_Y\in\mathbb R^{N\times T}\). Here \(B\) is the marker-effect matrix and
\(E_Y\) is the residual-observation matrix; neither symbol denotes a covariance
matrix.

The covariance notation is

| Quantity | ST | MT |
|---|---:|---:|
| active marker effects | \(v_b\) | \(V_b\) |
| genomic values | \(v_g\) | \(V_g\) |
| residuals | \(v_e\) | \(V_e\) |

For a non-null trait-activity pattern \(p\) and BayesR component \(k>0\), a
shared marker-specific variance multiplier gives

$$
\operatorname{Cov}(\beta_{j,p,k})
=\gamma_kq_jV_{b,p},
$$

where \(V_{b,p}\) is the active-trait submatrix of \(V_b\). The scalar \(q_j\)
rescales the complete active covariance matrix and therefore does not by itself
change the correlation structure represented by \(V_b\).

The current MT prior-state probability model depends on the core family:

- ordinary MT BayesR/SBayesR uses one `joint_pi` simplex over the unique null
  state and all non-null trait-pattern by positive-component states;
- MT BayesRC/SBayesRC factorizes marker component probability \(P\) from a
  global conditional non-null sharing probability \(H\).

The component and pattern probabilities reported for ordinary MT BayesR are
marginals of its full joint simplex; they are not parameters of a current
\(P\times H\) factorization. See [MT BayesR/SBayesR](mt_bayesr_sbayesr.qmd) and
[MT BayesRC/SBayesRC](mt_bayesrc_sbayesrc.qmd) for the implemented state spaces.

## Likelihood information and operators

The core prior family does not determine how the Gaussian likelihood is
evaluated:

- packed BED routes use selected individual-level genotypes;
- CSR routes use aligned summary cross-products and sparse LD;
- block-eigen routes use within-block spectral representations, either the
  canonical retained-factor form for current scalar fits or an explicitly
  reconstructed dense representation where supported.

The `S` prefix in names such as SBayesC and SBayesR identifies a
summary-statistics likelihood/display convention. It does not define a new
effect prior and does not activate MAF scaling. MAF-S behavior is controlled
separately by `maf_effect_s`.

For the underlying likelihood information, see
[Summary Statistics](summary_statistics.qmd) and
[Multi-Trait Sample Overlap](multitrait_overlap.qmd). For operator details, see
[Sparse-LD CSR](sparse_ld_csr.qmd) and
[Block-Eigen LD](block_eigen_operator.qmd).
